# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Friday, November 20, 2026

Edition for Friday, 20 November 2026 (IST), drafted on Friday morning from the 07:02–07:50 IST data pack and published on Friday evening after the market closed. Everything from "Urgent / High impact" down reflects that morning pack and keeps its own as-of dates: Thursday 19 Nov closes, the 19 Nov PM gold rate and the 20 Nov AGLOC block. The late update below carries the Friday 20 Nov close.

## 🕘 Late update — Friday 20 November close

Friday's session widened the gap the lead story describes. Nifty Bank rose 2.49% to 64,635.20, above Thursday's record close of 63,063.00; Nifty Financial Services gained 2.02% to 28,871.20 and Nifty NBFC 0.32% to 56,033.41, while the gold-loan lenders fell again — Muthoot Finance ₹2,550.50 (−2.58%), IIFL Finance ₹611.95 (−5.04%) and Manappuram Finance ₹280.50 (−0.83%). The Nifty 50 closed at 25,800.60 (+286.30, +1.12%).
Sources: [NSE index closes, 20 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/indices/ind_close_all_20112026.csv) · [NSE bhavcopy, 20 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/products/content/sec_bhavdata_full_20112026.csv)

Gold fell further. IBJA's 20 Nov PM rate for 999 purity was ₹12,389.3 a gram, ₹563.8 (−4.35%) below the 19 Nov PM session, and the 916 rate was ₹11,348.6. AGLOC's next dated block, for Monday 23 Nov, sets the 85% ceiling at ₹9,646 a gram, ₹439 below its 20 Nov block, with 80% at ₹9,078 and 75% at ₹8,511, on a jewellery reference of ₹11,348 (down ₹517).
Sources: [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/) · [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/)

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the ceiling that applies from Monday is ₹439 lower than the one that applied on Friday, so the same grams of pledged gold support a smaller maximum loan when the week opens. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp LTV or loan-book figure for 20 Nov.
Sources: [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/) · [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/)

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Gold-loan lenders lag a record market day as gold resumes its fall
On Thursday 19 Nov the Sensex rose 989.94 points (+1.21%) to 83,021.75, and Nifty Bank closed at a record 63,063.00 (+1.65%). The gold-loan lenders did not take part. Muthoot Finance (a listed peer, and not Muthoot Fincorp) fell 0.83% to ₹2,618.00, its second straight decline. Manappuram Finance slipped 0.05% to ₹282.85, and IIFL Finance fell 2.64% to ₹644.45. The Nifty NBFC index rose 0.04%, against 1.10% for Nifty Financial Services.

The gold price was the backdrop. MCX December gold futures settled at ₹1,29,770 per 10 g, down ₹44 (−0.03%). Comex December gold settled at $3,685.50 an ounce, down 1.51%, after a 3.16% fall the previous session. AGLOC's 85% LTV ceiling for 20 Nov fell ₹127 a gram to ₹10,085, and its jewellery reference fell ₹149 to ₹11,865. IBJA's 999 rate for the 19 Nov PM session was ₹12,953.1 a gram, down ₹163.3.

This is how the collateral mechanism works. A gold loan is capped at a share of the value of the gold pledged, the loan-to-value (LTV) ratio. AGLOC publishes that cap as a rupee figure per gram for each band: ₹10,085 at 85%, ₹9,492 at 80% and ₹8,898 at 75%, all set against a jewellery reference of ₹11,865. That reference equals IBJA's 916 (22-carat) rate for the 19 Nov PM session. When gold falls, the per-gram figures fall with it. For a loan already written close to its ceiling, the cushion becomes thinner. For fresh lending against the same grams, the maximum loan is smaller. The same pledged gold supports less debt than it did a day earlier.

Moneycontrol's 19 Nov report places the lenders' fall alongside the gold price. Its text says gold loan shares fell up to 2.6% on Thursday, and that gold prices remained near a 14-month low. The same report says Muthoot Finance has lost 31.8% year to date and Manappuram 10%, while IIFL Finance is up 4.1% for the year.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a lower gold price lowers the per-gram value of the collateral behind every gold loan, Muthoot Fincorp's included. Loans written close to an LTV ceiling have a thinner cushion, and the same grams support less new lending. The sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp loan-book or LTV figure for 19 Nov.

### Muthoot Microfin board approves special-purpose H1 statements for Muthoot Fincorp's restated IPO accounts
This is Muthoot Fincorp's own chain of events, and it is a filing-facilitation step, not a new result. The board meeting was intimated on 13 Nov and noted in the 18 Nov edition as due on Thursday 19 Nov. The outcome is now on NSE.

Muthoot Microfin, a group company, held its board meeting on 19 Nov 2026 (1:45–1:55 PM). The board approved audited special-purpose interim financial statements for the half years ended 30 September 2025 and 30 September 2026, with the statutory auditors' reports. The filing says these were prepared solely to facilitate the preparation of the Restated Consolidated Financial Statements of Muthoot Fincorp Limited, the holding company, for its proposed Initial Public Offering of equity shares. It confirms there is no change in the financial figures against the statutory results already filed under Regulation 33 and Regulation 52. The statements are not themselves statutory periodic results, so they were not enclosed. The NSE filing is timestamped 19 Nov 2026 14:00:57.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none on its reported figures, because the filing says the numbers are unchanged from what was already filed. It is a step in the IPO restatement work. The restated consolidated statements themselves, and the IPO price band and dates, are not in the sources checked.
Sources: [NSE: Muthoot Microfin outcome of board meeting, 19 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/muthootmicrofin_19112026140057_OutcomeofBoardMeeting19112026SD.pdf)

### CreditAccess Grameen closes at a 52-week low on triple its average volume, on a day the market rose
CreditAccess Grameen (CREDITACC), a microfinance lender, closed at ₹970.60 on Thursday 19 Nov, down ₹75.60 (−7.23%). It traded 13,54,663 shares, 3.0x its 30-session average volume, with delivery at 47.40%. The day's low was ₹965.70. The close is a fresh 52-week low; the previous 52-week high was ₹1,634.00 on 31 Jul 2026. The stock had already fallen 5.75% on 18 Nov, a two-session fall of about 12.5%.

The broad market rose the same day: Nifty 50 gained 1.14% and Nifty Bank closed at a record. No company-specific reason is established in the sources checked. Univest's 19 Nov note says explicitly that a company-specific reason has not been established. This edition does not attribute the move to any cause.

As an NBFC-sector dispersion datapoint, the same session had Five Star Business Finance up 2.18% (₹435.85) and Muthoot Microfin, a group company, up 2.80% (₹169.80).

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked. CreditAccess Grameen is a microfinance lender, not a gold-loan lender, and the sources give no link to Muthoot Fincorp's book.

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

Indian shares rose on Thursday 19 Nov. The Nifty 50 closed at 25,514.30 (+1.14%), above 25,500 for the first time in nearly nine months. Nifty PSU Bank rose 2.29%, Nifty Private Bank 1.39% and Nifty Auto 4.40%, with Maruti Suzuki (+7.58%) the top Nifty gainer. Nifty IT fell 1.10%, with TCS (−1.55%), Tech Mahindra (−1.54%) and Infosys (−1.52%) among the losers. India VIX closed at 16.11, up 3.50%. Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers of ₹7,411.41 crore on 19 Nov, and domestic institutions were net sellers of ₹1,356.57 crore (both NSE provisional).

The rupee closed at 93.36 to the dollar (provisional), up 5 paise, its fourth straight session of gains. The dollar index was 103.61, down 0.17%. Brent settled at $91.98 a barrel (ICE January 2027 contract, +0.03%).

## 📉 NPA & Asset Quality

### Analyst caution: falling gold prices shrink collateral cushions
Deven Choksey, managing director of DRChoksey Finserv, told CNBC-TV18 that he is cautious on Muthoot Finance (a listed peer) and Manappuram despite attractive valuations. He expects stress over the next couple of quarters as falling gold prices reduce the value of pledged collateral. He also flagged rural drought conditions and lenders rolling over old loans into fresh ones.

This is an analyst's view. It is not company guidance, and it is not a finding about either company's loan book. The CNBC-TV18 page is dated 18 Nov 2026 in its metadata, though its body text does not repeat the date.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the analyst's point runs through the same mechanism as the lead story, since lower gold values mean less collateral cover per loan. The newest Muthoot Fincorp asset-quality figures in the sources checked are from its Q2 filing of 14 Nov: Stage III 1.07%, against 1.41% a year earlier.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Friday, 20 November 2026 (IST)

Edition for Friday, 20 November 2026 (IST), published on Friday evening after the market closed. Covers Thursday 19 Nov to Friday evening.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 19 Nov changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp. What was checked is set out below. A representation to RBI is not a rule change, and the RBI liquidity operations under "Liquidity operations and other RBI releases" are operations, not rules.

## What was checked

What was checked between Thursday 19 Nov and Friday evening 20 Nov, with a second pass after the 20 Nov close: the RBI notifications feed, where the latest instrument is still the 11 Nov 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, with nothing new dated 19 or 20 Nov; the RBI press releases of 19 and 20 Nov, routine liquidity and debt-management items apart from the enforcement action set out below; SEBI's circular list, where the latest circular is still the one dated 17 Nov 2026 on the margin framework for the commodity derivatives segment, which is not NBFC lending, and no circular is dated 18, 19 or 20 Nov; and the IBBI site, whose footer reads "Last updated on: 16 Nov 2026" and which carries nothing dated 19 or 20 Nov.
Sources: [RBI notifications feed](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [SEBI circular, 17 Nov](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/review-of-margin-framework-for-commodity-derivatives-segment_105799.html) · [SEBI circular list](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0) · [IBBI](https://ibbi.gov.in/)

## Liquidity operations and other RBI releases (not rules)

- RBI overnight VRRR, 19 Nov (liquidity absorbed): the variable rate reverse repo auction notified ₹50,000 crore. Offers and acceptances were both ₹11,682 crore, at a cut-off and weighted average of 5.49%. This absorbed liquidity from the system.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1522](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64000)

- RBI 3-day VRR, 20 Nov (liquidity injected): a Variable Rate Repo auction under LAF of ₹50,000 crore, window 09:30–10:00 AM on 20 Nov, reversal on 23 Nov 2026 (Monday). The release gives its reason as "on a review of current and evolving liquidity conditions in the near term". A repo injects liquidity, which is the opposite direction from the VRRR above. This is an operation, not a rule.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none on any rule. The sources checked do not link this operation to Muthoot Fincorp's borrowing costs.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1525](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64003)

- Other RBI press releases of 19 Nov, all routine: an underwriting auction of ₹33,000 crore of government securities on 20 Nov (6.53% GS 2031 ₹19,000 crore; 7.71% GS 2066 ₹14,000 crore); a state government securities auction offering ₹31,950 crore (face value); Overseas Direct Investment for October 2026; Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions; and "Money Market Operations as on November 18, 2026", which is 18 Nov data and shows net absorption that day. None of these is a rule.
Sources: [Underwriting auction, prid=63999](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63999) · [State government securities auction, prid=64004](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64004) · [Overseas Direct Investment, prid=64001](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64001) · [Panchayati Raj finances, prid=64002](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64002) · [Money market operations, prid=63998](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63998)

## ⚖️ Enforcement action (not a rule change)

RBI's 20 Nov releases carried one enforcement item. By an order dated 17 Nov 2026, RBI imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh on Fusion Finance Limited for non-compliance with its KYC directions and its Internal Ombudsman directions. The order says the company failed to obtain PAN, an equivalent e-document or Form 60 from customers when establishing an account-based relationship, and failed to escalate partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time. It follows RBI's statutory inspection of the company as on 31 March 2026 and is stated to rest on deficiencies in regulatory compliance. The rest of the 20 Nov releases were operational: a 4-day VRR notified for 23 Nov, the result of a second 3-day VRR, conversion of state government securities, Treasury Bill auctions, the weekly statistical supplement and FAQs on the FEMA export and import regulations.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly, since the order is against another lender and changes no rule. The Internal Ombudsman obligation it cites is the one behind Muthoot Fincorp's own Oct–Dec quarterly return, due 15 Jan 2027.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1537, penalty on Fusion Finance, 20 Nov](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64015) · [RBI press release 2026-2027/1531, FEMA FAQs, 20 Nov](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64009) · [RBI press releases, 20 Nov](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx)

## Deadlines

Open circular threads due within 14 days: SEBI Credit Risk-o-Meter for debt offers (21 Nov) and RBI draft priority-sector lending Directions (comments by 26 Nov).

- **21 Nov 2026:** Credit Risk-o-Meter disclosure goes live for debt securities (SEBI HO/17/11/22(1)2026-DDHS-POD1) ([link](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/oct-2026/introduction-of-credit-risk-o-meter-as-an-additional-disclosure-mechanism-for-debt-securities_105081.html))

latest_circulars.title: RBI consolidates its Domestic Money Transfer Directions
latest_circulars.summary: RBI issued the Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026, which consolidate the existing DMT instructions for banks and authorised payment system operators and take effect immediately. Cash pay-outs stay capped at ₹10,000 a transaction and ₹25,000 a month per beneficiary, and walk-in remitters can send up to ₹5,000 a transaction and ₹25,000 a month through BCs, with registration on a verified mobile number and a self-certified OVD.
latest_circulars.impact: not addressed to NBFCs; it applies to an NBFC only where it acts for a bank or payment operator. The velocity checks and alerts on unusual credit spurts in paras 15–17 describe controls also relevant to cash-heavy lending.
